correctness.rationale: All four item partitions have one forced valuation type in the smaller group and its antipode in the larger group; the remaining two types are flexible. Exhausting this list proves the min-count iff criterion with a complete capacity argument, including boundary equality. Pigeonhole and a four-count obstruction yield exact universality. Multinomial exponential generating functions, fixed-q tail estimates, and a singular four-variate central limit theorem prove the probabilistic statements. A direct implementation of the original mixed-EF1 inequalities agreed on all 123,792 labeled profile/size comparisons for n=2..7; these computations corroborate rather than replace proof.

value.rationale: The finding pinpoints when adjustable group membership does and does not rescue EF1 with signed tastes: a universal boundary at one quarter of the population, accompanied by an explicit finite exact probability and nontrivial Gaussian critical window. These distinguish robustness in balanced groups from exponentially rare feasibility for a fixed smaller group. This quantifies a natural motivating gap beyond the monotone universality theorem, rather than merely enumerating a known isolated negative instance.
